payload.task_text:
The student affairs office is conducting a pilot study on whether nutrition awareness correlates with academic performance. The study focuses on two Environmental Economics and Ethics courses (course IDs 13 and 14) from the learning management system.

Start by reading the study_protocol.md file in the workspace to understand the research methodology and IRB requirements. Also review the nutritional_guidelines.csv and campus_dining_budget.json files for context on daily nutritional requirements and budget constraints.

Query the learning management system for enrollment and grade data from both courses. For each course, retrieve assignments with their point values and submission counts. Also gather student-level submission patterns, specifically looking at which students have late submissions and their average scores.

Query the cooking recipe database for healthy recipe categories, focusing on breakfast and lunch options. Retrieve all categories along with recipe counts per category.

Write a Python script called categorize_students.py that reads the submission data and categorizes students into three engagement tiers. Students with zero late submissions are "High" engagement, students with a late submission rate up to and including 25% are "Medium" engagement, and students above 25% late rate are "Low" engagement. Compute both the late rate and the average score using only graded submissions (submissions that have a non-null score); count each student once even if they appear in both courses, and deduplicate students across the two courses. For each tier, the student count is the number of students in the tier, the average score is the arithmetic mean of the per-student average scores (each student weighted equally, regardless of how many submissions they made), and the late submission rate is the arithmetic mean of the per-student late rates. Report the late submission rate as a decimal fraction between 0 and 1 (e.g. 0.25, not 25%). Run this script via the terminal and save the output as student_engagement.json containing an array of objects with fields tier, student_count, avg_score, and late_submission_rate.

Write a second Python script called design_meal_plans.py that reads the student_engagement.json and the nutritional_guidelines.csv, then designs meal plan recommendations for each tier. High engagement students get a "Control" plan with no special meals. Medium engagement students get a "Partial" plan with breakfast recommendations only. Low engagement students get a "Full Meal Plan" with both breakfast and lunch recommendations. The script should pull breakfast and lunch recipe categories from the cooking database results and estimate a daily cost based on the campus_dining_budget.json constraints. Run this script and save the output as meal_recommendations.json.

Create a cloud spreadsheet titled "Nutrition Study Data" with two sheets. The first sheet called "Student_Engagement" should have columns Tier, Student_Count, Avg_Score, and Late_Submission_Rate, with one row per tier (High, Medium, Low) sorted by tier name. The second sheet called "Meal_Plans" should have columns Tier, Intervention_Type, Recommended_Meals, and Estimated_Daily_Cost. High tier gets "Control" intervention with "None" for meals and cost 0. Medium tier gets "Partial" intervention with breakfast recipes listed and estimated cost from budget. Low tier gets "Full Meal Plan" intervention with breakfast and lunch recipes listed and estimated cost from budget. Write all numeric values as literal numbers in the spreadsheet cells (do not use formulas).

Create a knowledge base database titled "Wellness Pilot Program" with properties Student_Group (title), Intervention_Type (select with options Full Meal Plan, Partial, Control), Enrollment (number), Start_Date (date), and Status (select with options Planning, Active, Completed). Add three entries, one for each engagement tier. The High tier group has Control intervention with the count of high-engagement students, start date 2026-04-01, status Planning. The Medium tier group has Partial intervention with the count of medium-engagement students, same start date and status. The Low tier group has Full Meal Plan intervention with the count of low-engagement students, same start date and status. Use the literal date value 2026-04-01 for the Start_Date property.

Send an email to student_affairs@university.edu with subject "Nutrition-Academic Performance Study: Pilot Proposal" summarizing the study findings. The body should mention the three engagement tiers with their student counts and average scores, the proposed intervention types, and request approval to proceed with the pilot starting April 2026.

Send a second email to dining_services@university.edu with subject "Meal Plan Recommendations for Wellness Pilot" describing the meal plan requirements. Include the number of students needing full and partial meal plans, the recommended breakfast and lunch categories from the recipe database, and budget estimates per tier.

Finally, write a Python summary script called generate_summary.py that reads student_engagement.json and meal_recommendations.json, then produces a comprehensive text report. The report must explicitly state, for each of the three engagement tiers (High, Medium, Low), its student count and average score, and should describe the proposed interventions and per-tier budget estimates. Run this script and save the output as nutrition_study_summary.txt in the workspace. Also save a local Excel backup called Nutrition_Academic_Study.xlsx with two sheets matching the cloud spreadsheet structure: "Student_Engagement" with columns Tier, Student_Count, Avg_Score, Late_Submission_Rate, and "Meal_Plans" with columns Tier, Intervention_Type, Recommended_Meals, Estimated_Daily_Cost.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent completes the two-course study directly; do not dispatch sub-agents. Dynamically resolve the task workspace, read study_protocol.md, nutritional_guidelines.csv and campus_dining_budget.json, and keep large tool responses in runtime-unique files rather than chat.

Verify Canvas courses 13/EEE-2013J and 14/EEE-2014J and their assignment inventories. Call canvas_list_student_submissions(grouped=false,per_page=100,page=1) for each course, then issue every remaining literal page revealed by total_pages in native-parallel batches, using full_output_path when a result is oversized. Deduplicate by literal submission row.id, then by user_id across courses; use only non-null scores. In the same ready-source phase, call HowToCook for each of the ten required categories and retain exact recipe IDs/names/categories/descriptions/ingredients.

The main agent is sole owner of categorize_students.py, student_engagement.json, design_meal_plans.py and meal_recommendations.json. Compute per-student average and late fraction; High=0 late, Medium=(0,0.25], Low>0.25. Tier averages weight students equally and late rates remain 0-1. Apply High/Control/None/0, Medium/Partial/breakfast, Low/Full Meal Plan/breakfast+lunch using only verified recipe names and source budget. Run and read back both scripts/JSON files and freeze the three canonical tier rows with source/page/recipe controls.

Then perform all six independent outputs directly, batching ready calls:

- cloud spreadsheet `Nutrition Study Data`: exhaust title search first; create at most once on zero exact matches, reuse the retained ID on one, and block on multiple exact matches or an ambiguous create. Ensure exactly `Student_Engagement` and `Meal_Plans`, batch write through the retained ID, and read the complete ranges back;
- Notion database `Wellness Pilot Program`: exhaust exact-title search first; create at most once on zero exact matches, reuse one exact retained database, and block on multiple matches or an ambiguous create. Verify the exact schema/options, upsert exactly one High, Medium and Low page with canonical enrollments, date 2026-04-01 and Planning, then paginate and read the retained database/pages back;
- Nutrition_Academic_Study.xlsx with the exact two sheets and literal numbers, fully read back;
- at-most-once email to student_affairs@university.edu with exact pilot-proposal subject and all tier counts/averages/interventions;
- at-most-once email to dining_services@university.edu with exact meal-plan subject, full/partial counts, verified categories and tier costs;
- generate_summary.py and nutrition_study_summary.txt with explicit High/Medium/Low counts, averages, interventions and budgets, then read back.

For each email, paginate Sent search and read recipients before send and after retain. Final acceptance uses external cloud/Notion/email read-backs and exact local files; no writer, verification or repair agents are allowed.

nodes.text:
You are gathering data from a Canvas LMS for a nutrition-academic performance study. You have Canvas read tools. Do NOT modify anything.

GOAL: Collect complete enrollment, assignment, and submission data for Canvas course ID 13 and course ID 14 (both "Environmental Economics and Ethics" courses).

STEPS:
1. Get course details for course 13 and course 14 (canvas_get_course) — record id, name, course_code.
2. List enrolled students per course (canvas_list_course_users and/or canvas_get_course_grades with type StudentEnrollment). Record each student's id, name, and enrollment role. Note which students appear in BOTH courses (overlapping enrollments matter — we must dedupe by student id).
3. List all assignments per course (canvas_list_assignments). Record assignment id, name, points_possible, and the number of submissions for each assignment (computed from submission data in step 4, or via canvas_list_assignment_submissions if needed).
4. Get ALL student submissions for all assignments in each course. Prefer canvas_list_student_submissions(course_id, per_page=100, page=1,2,...) — follow pagination until has_more is false. For each submission record: course_id, student_id, assignment_id, score (may be null), whether it is late (the `late` flag and/or workflow_state == 'late'), and workflow_state.
5. Identify which individual students have at least one late submission, and each student's average score across graded submissions (score not null).

RETURN FORMAT (compact, machine-readable — this is the most important part; keep it terse, no extra prose around the JSON except a 2-3 line summary):
Return ONE JSON object exactly like this structure, with ALL rows included (do not truncate; if it is huge, submissions may be arrays):
{
  "courses": [{"id": 13, "name": "...", "code": "..."}, ...],
  "students": {"13": [{"id": <int>, "name": "..."}, ...], "14": [...]},
  "overlap_student_ids": [<ids enrolled in both courses>],
  "assignments": {"13": [{"id": <int>, "name": "...", "points_possible": <num>, "submission_count": <int>}, ...], "14": [...]},
  "submissions": [[<course_id>, <student_id>, <assignment_id>, <score or null>, <late true/false>, "<workflow_state>"], ...]
}
Use compact single-line arrays for submissions to minimize size. Verify submission totals: report total submission row count per course.
Gather Canvas course 13/14 data

You are gathering data from a Chinese cooking recipe database (HowToCook MCP) for a university nutrition study designing breakfast + lunch meal plans. You have these tools: mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getAllRecipes, mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory, mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById, mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_recommendMeals, mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_whatToEat. Do NOT modify anything; read-only.

GOAL:
1. Retrieve ALL recipe categories along with recipe counts per category. The known categories are: 水产 (seafood), 早餐 (breakfast), 调料 (condiments), 甜品 (desserts), 饮品 (drinks), 荤菜 (meat dishes), 半成品加工 (semi-prepared), 汤 (soups), 主食 (staples), 素菜 (vegetable dishes). You can get counts by calling getRecipesByCategory for each category, or by calling getAllRecipes and counting. Report the count for EACH category.
2. Breakfast focus: list ALL recipes in the 早餐 (breakfast) category with id + name. Pick 3-4 healthy breakfast recipes and get their details (main ingredients, servings) via getRecipeById — keep details concise (ingredients list only, no full step text).
3. Lunch focus: there is no explicit lunch category; healthy lunch options should come from 荤菜 (meat), 素菜 (vegetable), 汤 (soup), 主食 (staples). From each of those categories list up to 5 example recipe names (id + name), and pick 3-4 overall healthy lunch-suitable recipes and get concise ingredient details for them.

RETURN FORMAT (compact machine-readable JSON, most important):
{
  "categories": [{"name_zh": "早餐", "name_en": "breakfast", "count": <int>}, ...ALL 10 categories...],
  "breakfast_recipes": [{"id": <int>, "name": "..."}, ...all of them...],
  "breakfast_picks": [{"id": <int>, "name": "...", "ingredients": ["...","..."]}, ...3-4...],
  "lunch_candidates": {"荤菜": [{"id":..,"name":".."}, up to 5], "素菜": [...], "汤": [...], "主食": [...]},
  "lunch_picks": [{"id": <int>, "name": "...", "category": "荤菜", "ingredients": [...]}, ...3-4...]
}
Include exact recipe ids as returned by the API. Keep everything terse so it fits in one message.
Gather recipe category data
